method_note: These are documented internal NP discussions, recommendations, and organizing actions. A discussion item is not treated as unanimous member agreement unless the source says so. Kessler's personal recommendation is identified as such.

records.action: Lucas circulated a racial-reconciliation resolution through the NP; Kessler called it a step in the right direction and created a discussion page; Lucas said the proposal recognized covenantal and generational involvement and complicity in racial injustice and had been circulated through key Black PCA pastors/RAAN before moving forward.
Kessler urged NP members to be present for the two-thirds vote required to refer the racial-reconciliation resolution to the Overtures Committee.

Post-Assembly, Kessler said the racial-reconciliation overture would require more NP work and thanked Richter for work on an overture intended to address racial injustice without frustrating emerging African American leadership.

NP correspondence states Lucas and Duncan co-authored the earlier resolution. Kessler preferred the covenantal-responsibility approach of Overtures 4/6 and urged members to move identical forms or affirmations through their presbyteries.
Kessler described the revised racial-reconciliation overture as a first step of recognition and repentance.
Kessler celebrated the Racial Reconciliation Study Committee and its intention to move from report to specific actions.

NP circulated and discussed the Cooperative Ministries Committee recommendation for a study committee on women serving in the church, including ordination, deacons/deaconesses, and differing current practices.
Kessler explicitly stated strong support for the proposed women-in-ministry study committee and urged NP members to join the discussion.

After the Administrative Committee of Commissioners opposed the study committee, Kessler urged full engagement on the floor in favor of establishing it. Rowan supplied a pro-study-committee summary circulated by Kessler.
Kessler explicitly identified Ince as an NP member and chairman of the Women Serving in Ministry committee and circulated Ince's internal introduction to the committee's makeup, goals, and work.
Kessler identified allowing unordained persons, including women, to serve as voting members on PCA boards/agencies as one of three goals worth significant effort at the 2019 Assembly.

NP maintained discussion pages for Westminster Presbytery overtures concerning homosexuality and same-sex marriage. A later briefing described a divided Overtures Committee debate between those seeking a denominational public statement and those who considered such statements pastorally unhelpful in local cultural engagement.

Kessler recommended defeating a Nashville Statement-focused approach and instead pursuing a narrowly defined study committee on homosexual desire and ministry to people experiencing same-sex attraction. He wrote that Revoice existed in part because the PCA's prior strategy had functioned as 'don't ask-don't tell.'

An internal message asked for a South City St. Louis / Revoice Board participant to be added to the NP group. The person's identity should be promoted only after the surrounding archive text is fully normalized.
Kessler circulated Sauls's public essay on Revoice and PCA division as an encouraging clarification of the controversy.

Kessler reported vigorous debate by many NP-connected commissioners against treating the Nashville Statement as a needed stand-alone Assembly proclamation without prominent pastoral guidance, while noting the committee nevertheless approved it.
NP correspondence discussed the Human Sexuality report's treatment of continued same-sex attraction and circulated Tim LeCroy's essay on homosexuality in the PCA as well done.
In committee-candidate advice, Kessler preferred candidates he viewed as more open to strong fraternal ties and wrote that he saw value in continued NAE ties.

Kessler circulated and explicitly agreed with O'Neil's argument against a proposal for PCA withdrawal from the NAE. O'Neil cited PCA theological influence within the NAE and Roy Taylor's long service as NAE board chairman.
Kessler repeatedly identified defeating proposed NAE withdrawal as an NP Assembly goal and directed members to be present for the relevant floor action.
An NP email encouraged additional overtures following child-protection work so that those hesitant to speak to legal or so-called social-justice issues would see a stronger PCA message.
NP recommended a seminar framing presbytery-culture transformation as a means toward church planting, mercy ministry, and community transformation.
The racial-reconciliation resolution circulated through NP explicitly used justice/mercy language concerning the Civil Rights era and local confession/reconciliation.

issues.research_note: An exact-term scan of the combined NP archive on 2026-09-03 found no literal matches for immigrant, migrant, refugee, or refugees. This is not evidence that the subject is absent; semantic and external-source research remains pending. A Faithful PCA's 2021 letter explicitly praised refugee care, so that coalition should be researched separately from NP.
